chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked him about two men who married two women, and this one was brought the wife of that one, and that one was brought the wife of this one. He said: 'This one observes the waiting period from this one, and this one from this one, then each of them returns to her husband.'
And he said regarding a man who marries a woman and tells her, 'I am from so-and-so's family,' but it is not so: He said: 'He annuls the marriage,' or he said: 'He returns the marriage.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marriage validity when there is a mistake in identity or lineage?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in marital status, ruling that mistaken identity does not invalidate the current marriage, allowing the women to complete their *iddah* before returning to their original spouses. It further establishes that misrepresentation of lineage (*tadlis*) constitutes a defect (*'ibbah*) giving the wife the option to annul (*faskh*) or return the marriage, reflecting the Shia emphasis on consent and accuracy in contractual terms.
